content: The information provided was last updated in August 2024. It is important to note that this document is a summary and does not include all possible details about the medication. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. This medication, commonly known under the brand name Harvoni, is a combination of ledipasvir and sofosbuvir. It is used to treat chronic hepatitis C, a viral infection of the liver. In some cases, it may be used in combination with another antiviral medication, ribavirin. These drugs work by reducing the amount of hepatitis C virus in the body, which helps the immune system fight the infection and may aid in liver recovery. However, it is not known if this treatment prevents the transmission of the virus to others. Warning: While this medication is used to treat hepatitis C, it may rarely exacerbate another liver condition called hepatitis B. Before starting this medication, inform your doctor if you have ever had hepatitis B. How to Use: Read the patient information leaflet and instructions provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If using the pellet form, gently shake the packet before use. To take it without food, open the packet and pour the pellets directly into your mouth. Swallow the pellets without chewing, and you may drink water afterward if needed. If your dose requires more than one packet, repeat these steps. If taking the medication with food, pour the pellets into a small bowl with one or more spoonfuls of non-acidic soft food (e.g., pudding, mashed potatoes, or ice cream) at or below room temperature. This medication works best when the drug level in your body is kept constant. Take it at evenly spaced intervals. If you vomit within 5 hours of taking the medication, inform your doctor. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a short time. Interactions with Other Medications: Antacids can reduce the absorption of ledipasvir. Other acid-lowering medications for indigestion, heartburn, or ulcers (e.g., famotidine, omeprazole) may interfere with the effectiveness of ledipasvir. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Side Effects: Common side effects may include tiredness, headache, nausea, diarrhea, or difficulty sleeping. Serious allergic reactions are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. Contact your doctor for medical advice if you experience any concerning symptoms. Precautions: Before taking this medication, inform your doctor if you are allergic to ledipasvir, sofosbuvir, or any other ingredients in the product. If you have diabetes, hepatitis C treatment may lower your blood sugar levels, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Your doctor may adjust your diabetes treatment plan accordingly. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, when combined with ribavirin, must not be used during pregnancy by either the pregnant woman or her male partner, as it may harm an unborn baby. Reliable birth control methods must be used during treatment and for a specified period afterward (9 months for female patients and 6 months for male patients). Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 6 hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Keep tablets in their original container. Do not open pellet packets until ready to use. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Overdose: In case of overdose with serious symptoms (e.g., passing out or trouble breathing), call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring: Laboratory tests (e.g., liver function, hepatitis B and C tests) should be conducted before, during, and after treatment. If using this medication with ribavirin, female patients or female partners of male patients should take a pregnancy test before starting treatment. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions and discuss any concerns or questions you may have about this medication.
